comments.body:
Change 2670 pushed: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2670 (`715d62a8d9e0`). Two files, as declared in file_impact — no widening.

## AC-by-AC

**AC1 — assertions honour admission again.** Re-applied the intent of `6125c5345f01`:
`assert "new=0" in out or "admitted" in out` and `assert set(baseline) | admitted == live`
(`admitted = set(ratchet.markers_for(REPO_ROOT))`). One deliberate improvement on the original:
`increased=0` is kept as its OWN assertion rather than folded into the `or`. `6125c534`'s form
widened the first condition and thereby dropped the increase check entirely; re-applying it
verbatim would have re-introduced that hole.

**AC2 — the pin (the point of the ticket).** `test_the_committed_tree_assertions_consult_marker_admission`
pins both committed-tree assertions to consult admission. Two design decisions worth recording:

- *Source-level, not behavioural.* The behavioural alternative — assert the tree currently holds a
  marker-admitted, non-baselined mechanism — only detects the regression while such an example
  survives, and keeping one alive would mean forbidding its removal. That fights the shrink-only
  ratchet, whose entire purpose is to reward deletion. Rejected on those grounds.
- *AST, not text.* My first draft matched on source text and I caught it failing open during
  seeding: reverting an assertion while leaving its explanatory comment in place still contains the
  word "admitted", so the text pin passed over a genuinely reverted assertion. Rewritten to walk
  `ast.parse` output, where comments do not exist. Recording this because a text pin here looks
  correct and is not.

**AC3 — contributor path end to end.** Added a scratch `scripts/check_ac3_scratch.py` carrying only
a `# mechanism-ok:` marker, no baseline edit:

    --check:  active=680 new=3 increased=0 stale=0
              admitted  ci_gate::scripts/check_ac3_scratch.py — ticket affd-913c...
              exit=0
    pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py:  33 passed

Scratch file removed afterwards; not in the change.

**AC4 — VERDICT: the two lines ARE removable, and are removed.** With admission honoured, the full
module is 33 passed without them. They were bookkeeping for the defect, not justification — the
markers in `scripts/check_terraform_tree_currency.py` and the terraform-drift workflow carry the
justification themselves, and `--check` reports both as `admitted`. Grepped for other consumers:
only `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` reads the baseline for assertions, and this change does
not alter `--check` behaviour at all, so no doc statement goes stale.

**AC5 — out of scope by design**, tracked as `fleece-foliated-dotterel` (`4c95-637a-a2d3-454c`).

## Seeded-defect results

Both directions, each with the explanatory comment left in place (the case that defeated the text
pin):

| seed | result |
|---|---|
| revert assertion 1 (`test_check_passes_on_the_committed_tree`) | **2 failed**, 31 passed |
| revert assertion 2 (`test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_live_tree`) | **2 failed**, 31 passed |

Two failures each time: the seeded assertion itself, plus the pin naming it. Before the fix, the pin
alone was RED on unmodified `origin/main` `9d5a7278c892` with the defect-naming message — i.e. the
new check fails against current main ONLY because of the defect being fixed, which is the permitted
carve-out.

## Gates

`make lint` PASS (after two self-inflicted fixes: E501, then `ruff format`). `make typecheck` PASS,
765 files. Complexity ratchet `active=33 new=0 increased=0 stale=16`, exit 0.

**Mechanism ratchet: `active=680 new=2 increased=0 stale=0`, exit 0, both lines `admitted`.** Worth
being precise since "new=0" was the stated bar: this change does not ADD a mechanism, it moves two
from baseline bookkeeping to marker admission. `new=2 admitted / exit 0` IS the designed
green-at-rest state for a marker-admitted mechanism — it is the state this change exists to make
the tests agree with. A literal `new=0` here would mean the fix had not worked.

## Suites run

Host load 31.7 (1-min) on 18 cores, above the ~25 threshold, so targeted rather than full
`make verify`: `test_mechanism_delta.py`, `test_terraform_drift_workflow_shape.py`,
`test_terraform_tree_currency.py`, `test_tests_import_convention.py` — 56 passed, 2 skipped. Bare
`pytest` console script throughout. CI carries the full suite.

No gate refusals. Not submitted, not closed.

compiled_state.description:
## The defect

`tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` no longer honours `# mechanism-ok:` markers. A contributor
with a CORRECT, matching marker still fails the test suite and has no sanctioned path forward,
because `--update-stale` refuses to write while anything is new and `AGENTS.md` forbids hand-editing
`.github/mechanism-baseline.json`.

## Proven by experiment, not inferred

Fresh worktree at `origin/main` `9d5a7278c892`. Deleting exactly the two baseline lines that change
2658 added, and nothing else:

    python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check
      active=680 new=2 increased=0 stale=0
        admitted  ci_gate::.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml::Assert this tree is current...
        admitted  ci_gate::scripts/check_terraform_tree_currency.py — bug eebc-6aa1-e45b-4325
      exit=0                                   <- markers MATCHED, gate GREEN

    pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py
      2 failed, 30 passed                      <- the TESTS disagree with the gate

Restoring the two baseline lines: 32 passed. So the markers are well-formed and the ratchet script
admits them; only the tests are blind to admission.

## Root cause: a contract that existed only inside a revertable commit

`git log -S'admitted'` on that test file returns exactly two commits:

- **`6125c5345f01`** "Pin review scanner contracts in Verified" — ADDED the marker-honouring forms
  (`assert "new=0" in out or "admitted" in out`, and `assert set(baseline) | admitted == live`).
  It had to: it introduced two new `ci_gate` mechanisms of its own.
- **`9c7d78127696`** "Revert scanner-integration Verified gate" — reverted `6125c534` WHOLESALE for
  reasons that had nothing to do with the ratchet (a vacuous `Verified` vote and a red required job
  blocking every open change). **The revert took the marker-honouring assertions with it.**

Current main reads `assert "new=0" in out and "increased=0" in out` (line 94) and
`assert set(baseline) == live` (line 358) — the pre-marker forms.

## Why this matters more than the immediate breakage

The marker contract was only ever expressed INSIDE a commit that was revertable for other reasons,
so **nothing detected its loss**. A wholesale revert is a legitimate operation; the defect is that a
cross-cutting contract had no independent existence to survive one. The fix is a re-application, not
a design — `markers_for` still exists and is exported from `check_mechanism_delta.py`.

It also explains a documented confusion: ticket `celadon-computable-smelts` (`a1f1-a30d-2d50-4f5a`)
was filed on this premise, RETRACTED as a false premise (correctly, at the time), and is now true
again. Its own AC2 note observed that the workflow had been reverted and concluded the *proof* was
stale — the missed step was that the *assertions* went with it.

## Related but distinct

`a1f1`'s current ACs describe **silent non-admission**: a marker on an unmatched key is entirely
ignored (`_partition` in `scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py` reads `markers.get(key, "")`, and
`_blank_marker_errors` reports only BLANK reasons, so a non-blank marker on a wrong key is never
named). That is real and confirmed by construction — but it is NOT what bit change 2658, whose
markers matched. Keep the two separate: this ticket is the blocker, that one is a DX improvement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` honours marker admission again, re-applying the intent of
      `6125c5345f01` rather than inventing a new mechanism. Proven by the experiment above: delete
      2658's two baseline lines and the module passes on the strength of the markers alone.
- [ ] A regression test pins the TESTS THEMSELVES to honour markers, so a future wholesale revert of
      an unrelated commit cannot silently remove the contract again. This is the point of the ticket
      — without it the same loss recurs the next time a scanner change is reverted.
- [ ] The contributor path is verifiable end to end: a new justified mechanism with a correct marker
      passes `--check` AND the test suite, with no baseline hand-edit. Proven by adding one in a
      scratch tree and running both.
- [ ] `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` entries added as workarounds are reviewed: change 2658's two
      lines should be removable once this lands. Confirm they are, or state why they must stay.
- [ ] The scope of what else `9c7d78127696` dropped is established separately (it touched 12 files
      including `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` and four test files). Do NOT assume the ratchet was
      the only casualty; that audit is its own ticket.

file_impact.reason: the two marker-blind assertions (line 94 test_check_passes_on_the_committed_tree, line 358 test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_live_tree) are re-pointed at marker admission, re-applying the intent of 6125c5345f01; and the new regression test that pins those two assertions to consult admission is added here, beside what it guards

AC4: change 2658 added two ci_gate lines (terraform-drift workflow step and check_terraform_tree_currency.py) purely as a workaround for the marker-blind assertions. Once markers are honoured they are redundant and are removed, so the committed tree stops carrying a workaround whose cause is fixed

compiled_state.title: test_mechanism_delta.py stopped honouring mechanism-ok markers: a wholesale revert of an unrelated scanner commit took the marker-honouring assertions with it, so a correct marker still fails the suite
